body:
[A114] Status navigation added; recorded acceptance criteria preserved.

## Current navigation (2026-09-14)

**Status: On Hold.** Physical acceptance is deferred by the owner to [I2S and TDM physical validation](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/milestone/9), due December 31, 2026. Suitable pin-measurement equipment is currently unavailable. [#448](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/448) coordinates the deferred I2S/TDM bench work. Acceptance 4 stays open; digital acceptance and its existing evidence remain recorded below.

 The [recorded decision](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/386#issuecomment-5604974838) selects the common-point setpoint law. Digital acceptance **1, 2, 3 and 5** was delivered by [PR #435](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/435). The [explicit reopening](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/386#issuecomment-5646136934) keeps **acceptance 4 open**: same-sample wire-to-TDM-pin measurement on the identified booted image under INTERNAL and CRF, with the required evidence and band.

The [current dependency update](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/386#issuecomment-5670905628) identifies [#447](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/447) as the necessary physical renderer implementation. Its reviewed merge enables this measurement; it does not complete acceptance 4. Physical qualification follows [#117's accepted one-DUT decision](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/117#issuecomment-5561827955): one AX7101 DUT against the validated reference peer.

Ownership: the [completed digital assignment](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/386#issuecomment-5604995192) was A104 with R105/R106. [#447's implementation](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/447#issuecomment-5669336955) is assigned to A119 with R151/R152; those are dependency roles. No separate executor/reviewer assignment for #386's remaining physical measurement is recorded in this issue's current body or updates.

The acceptance criteria and historical body below are preserved verbatim. Read their earlier Backlog, unassigned-role and two-board wording with the controlling decisions linked above.

---


Drafted from the README product roadmap, phase P1 "close the fabric roadmap" (README.md lines 329 to 333: deterministic listener latency, the setpoint law, the 0x002E reference). No open issue owns it at dev f46215cf; #36 (closed) owned the talker-side pipeline only.

## Objective and evidence

The listener's accept-to-render latency must be one constant, chosen at the packetization floor, identical for every selected clock source, and measured on the shipping image. Today the law exists for one render path and not for the one that ships.

- The setpoint law is implemented in `hdl/ieee1722/aaf/KL_i2s_playback.sv` lines 53 to 58 and 181 to 201: the steady-state fill is `SETPOINT_P`, the convergence and reset bands scale with it, and the prefill release defaults to the setpoint. `hdl/milan/milan_datapath.sv` lines 5620 to 5630 derive `SETPOINT_P = (6 * 2) + 4` from the class-A frame shape (one frame of 6 events by 2 samples plus a 4-sample CDC allowance: 16 samples, about 167 us at 48 kHz) and record the rule as "constant source-invariant latency, samples picked as soon as possible" (task #28).
- That block is pruned on the shipping shape. `configs/endstation_ax7101_1x1_tdm8.yaml` line 35 sets `i2s_playback: false` (`I2SPB_P = 0`, `milan_datapath.sv` line 5599), so the AX7101 renders through `KL_chan_map_render` and `KL_tdm_render`. `hdl/ieee1722/aaf/KL_chan_map_render.sv` lines 12 to 20 describe that path as a latest-sample latch, "free-running, no media queueing (the physical outputs run on their own 48 kHz tick; slips follow the house free-run rule)"; `hdl/ieee1722/aaf/KL_tdm_render.sv` lines 11 to 15 add a whole-frame double buffer into the TDM bit-clock domain. No setpoint, band or fill exists on this path; its accept-to-render delay is whatever phase the latch holds against the tick.
- The instruments stop short of the render. `docs/AAF_LATENCY_TAPS.md` lines 1 to 12 (the `0x870` taps) measure the wire-to-fabric-render stages and line 24 says the final playout stage is characterised separately by `I2SPB_STAT`, which the shipping shape reads as structural zero (`docs/reference/REGISTER_MAP.md` line 252). `AVTPRX_TSD` `0x6EC` (REGISTER_MAP.md line 1125; `docs/design/TIME_SYNC.md` lines 126 to 132) gives the presentation margin at accept, not the render delay.
- The compliance matrix records the silicon claim "latency = presentation offset" for IEEE 1722-2016 4.4.4.5, 4.4.4.9 and 4.3.2 (`docs/reference/MILAN_COMPLIANCE_MATRIX.md` lines 207 and 210). That is the end-to-end figure measured on the I2S shape, not the render delay of the TDM shape.
- The README names a `0x002E` reference. No tracked page resolves it; `docs/history/v1/reference/PROTOCOL_TRACEABILITY.md` line 325 is the only tracked record of the setpoint work ("task #28 packetization-floor setpoint in progress"). The lane records which VERSION carried the setpoint and corrects the README pointer.

## Authority and scope

- Milan v1.2 4.4.2.1, 4.4.2.3, 5.3.7.6, 5.3.8.10 with Table 5.6; IEEE 1722-2016 4.3.2 and 4.4.4.9. The constant-latency rule itself is a project rule (`milan_datapath.sv` lines 5623 to 5629), not a clause.
- REQUIREMENTS.md REQ-VER-05; docs/design/TIME_SYNC.md; docs/AAF_LATENCY_TAPS.md; docs/CHANNEL_MAP_64.md.
- Context: `KL_chan_map_render.sv`, `KL_tdm_render.sv`, `KL_i2s_playback.sv` lines 181 to 201, `milan_datapath.sv` lines 5599 to 5660, `tb/verilator/chmap_render`, `tb/verilator/tdm_render`, `tb/verilator/milan_dp` (`obj_aclk` true-ratio leg).
- A design decision first, recorded here before any edit: the latency law for the TDM render path. Either (a) the render crossbar gains the same setpoint element the I2S path has (a bounded elastic stage whose fill is the constant, prefill equal to the setpoint, recenter on a PHC step), or (b) the latest-sample latch is declared the law, its delay bounded to one media tick plus the depacketizer beat, and the README wording changes to match. The RTL or the documentation then follows the decision.

Out of scope: the talker pipeline (#36, closed); the clock-source actuators and grid alignment (#74); the stream restart delay (#75); any change to the presentation-time offset default (5.3.7.6).

## Acceptance and validation

1. The decision is recorded on this issue, with the constant stated in samples and microseconds at 48 kHz and derived from the frame shape, not mirrored as a literal.
2. `tb/verilator/milan_dp` measures accept-to-render delay on the elaborated 1x1 TDM8 shape for INTERNAL and for CRF selection at the true 391/1591 audio ratio and asserts one constant within the declared jitter band; a negative control (a deliberately wrong prefill) fails the check.
3. A GM identity change or PHC step during a locked stream returns the delay to the constant through one declared recenter, counted once, never a drift back at the residual rate (the `KL_i2s_playback.sv` lines 325 to 333 rule applied to the shipping path).
4. On the booted AX7101 image the delay is measured at the TDM frame pin against the wire arrival of the same sample (tap host capture plus the `0x870` taps), for a bound stream at INTERNAL and at CRF, and matches item 2 within the band; VERSION, image hash, numbers and capture are retained per docs/testing/TESTING.md 6b.
5. README.md's roadmap entry names the VERSION that carried the setpoint and drops or corrects the `0x002E` pointer; `python3 -B scripts/docs_check.py` and `scripts/check_feature_status.py --self-test` pass; Yosys and Verilator gates green on the exact candidate.

## Lane and review

Executor: unassigned. Independent reviewer: unassigned. Assigned by the manager when the lane opens.

Dependencies: #74 for the silicon grid probe and the CRF arm of item 2; #117 for a two-board bench with a tap host. Lane conflicts: any branch touching `KL_chan_map_render.sv`, `KL_tdm_render.sv` or the `milan_dp` audio legs (#367 and the #365 follow-ups).

Unresolved decisions: the render-path law above. Backlog until it is recorded.

comments.body:
> A design decision first, recorded here before any edit: the latency law for the TDM render path. Either (a) the render crossbar gains the same setpoint element the I2S path has (a bounded elastic stage whose fill is the constant, prefill equal to the setpoint, recenter on a PHC step), or (b) the latest-sample latch is declared the law, its delay bounded to one media tick plus the depacketizer beat, and the README wording changes to match. The RTL or the documentation then follows the decision.

Choosing a common point independent of the audio interface, but show accurate value, with no variation. If the delay from the audio interface or to the audio interface to the set point is known in advance and fixed, it's okay. BUt it needs to be accounted in the maths later in software.

[A10] Decision recorded from the owner's reply above: option (a), with the reference point defined. The shipping TDM render path gains the setpoint element the I2S path has: a bounded elastic stage whose fill is the constant, prefilled to the setpoint, re-centred on a PHC step. The latency law is stated at one common point independent of the audio interface (the render crossbar's input grid), so the value is accurate and shows no variation; the fixed, known delay from that point to each audio interface (TDM frame pin, I2S) is documented as a constant per interface so that software can account for it. The lane opens after #390's ring decision is folded in, since both touch the render chain.

[A10] Assignment for #386, under the recorded decision (option a)

Executor: A104. Independent reviewers: R105 (cleared context) and R106 (external to the lane). Branch `386-tdm-render-setpoint`, cut from `dev` at `9812e47d0789cedc353b2574374d15a3b7592b2b`.

Scope: the shipping TDM render path gains a bounded elastic stage whose fill is the constant setpoint, prefilled to the setpoint, re-centred on a PHC step, with the setpoint derived from the class-A frame shape the way the I2S path derives it (never a mirrored literal). The latency law is stated at the render crossbar's input grid, independent of the audio interface, and the fixed delay from that point to each interface is documented as a constant per interface. Acceptance 1, 2, 3 and 5 of the body in this lane (decision record with the constant in samples and microseconds, the milan_dp measurement at INTERNAL and CRF with a negative control, the single counted re-centre on a PHC step, the README pointer); acceptance 4 (the booted-board measurement at the TDM frame pin) rides the #117 bench. Lane conflicts: #390 (render chain, prefill constant) and #367 follow-ups; whichever lands second rebases.

Validation: the changed Verilator suites and the complete sweep, lint and xvlog ratchets, the docs gates, one OOC synthesis of the changed module recording the cell delta, then the local workflow replica, hosted required contexts, two positive five-lens reviews and post-merge containment.

[A10] Merged into dev as f7e25d6d59f584c64a3aa53586c08a83d62e2ab3 with R105-3 (cleared context) and R106-3 (external) FINISHED POSITIVE at 6a9769863622d79feaf82e3f53afa7c13698dfdc; every lens covered clean at that head by both rounds (ledgers published above), after six rounds that closed a bare-metal scope wording, a boundary naming ratchet, a test-evidence ratchet, a render delay that could sit one event off the setpoint after a live clock-source change, a pop that could tear an event handed to the crossbar, a lane-count mismatch on an odd channel count, and a per-interface delay row priced at the wrong bit clock.

Gate bar at the exact head: native bank 9 of 9, local workflow replica 4 of 4 workflows PASS, hosted required contexts 20 pass with 1 skipped.

Candidate merge: the base had moved twice since this head's merge base, so the candidate tree was built from the live tip and the reviewed head and gated before pressing merge, as CONTRIBUTING.md 2.1 step 7 requires. The intervening dev changes touch two files this change also touches, docs/testing/TESTING.md and sw/builder/test_builder.py, and the merge of those is what the candidate bank covered: nine of nine gates exit 0 on candidate tree e2e78d4e5a75e4593ee77d38cc52789eaac0c06b. The merge commit's tree is that same object, so what merged is what was gated.

Post-merge from the trusted checkout at f7e25d6d: check_merge_containment.py origin/386-tdm-render-setpoint exit 0 (contained), --merged-prs exit 0 (last 20 contained), check_merge_review_integrity.py exit 0 (clean over the last 20 merged PRs). Issue #386 keeps its acceptance 4 open, which rides the field campaign on #117; the recorded limitations (the settle rule's residual on the ceiling arm, the channel-count window, and the question of whether the shipped render prefill is twice its intended level, raised on this PR for the owning lane) stay in the body.

[A10] Reopened. The merge of PR #435 closed this issue automatically through the linked-branch connection made when the PR was opened, not through a closing keyword: the PR body says "Part of #386" and states in the same line that the issue stays open until the booted-board measurement is recorded.

What the merge delivered: acceptance 1, 2, 3 and 5. The setpoint is derived from the class-A frame shape and stated at the crossbar's input grid; the true-ratio leg measures one constant accept-to-render delay at INTERNAL and at CRF with its negative controls; a grandmaster change or a clock step returns the delay through one counted recentre, and so now does a live clock-source change; the per-interface delays are documented as fixed numbers with their derivations; the roadmap pointer names the VERSION that carried the setpoint.

What is left is acceptance 4 alone: on the booted AX7101 image, the delay measured at the TDM frame pin against the wire arrival of the same sample, for a bound stream at INTERNAL and at CRF, matching item 2 within the band, with VERSION, image hash, numbers and capture retained. That is a bench run on the hardware and it rides the field campaign of #117; it is not something the merged change can close by itself.

The board card returns to In progress for that reason. When the bench measurement is recorded here, the issue closes on its own evidence rather than on a link.

[A114] The missing physical TDM render path is now scoped in #447, a necessary implementation dependency of the remaining board acceptance here. It retains the existing shipping TDM8 MASTER role and #386's common-point law. The work must supply live serial timing and consistent descriptor/physical-key/slot mapping; enabling a count of eight alone misroutes two channels.

Executor [A119], independent reviewers [R151]/[R152]. The contract includes decoded serial sample evidence through the real mapping and audio path, followed by the full validation/review/merge bar. It remains Ready pending lane preparation. This implementation enables the measurement; it does not replace or complete this issue's physical acceptance.

[A114] Necessary dependency is In progress

#447's isolated implementation is running under its [recorded construction and correction obligations](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/447#issuecomment-5669336955). It must pass exact-head validation, both independent reviews and merge checks before an image can support this issue's measurement.

Acceptance 4 remains open. The capture driver is restored, while the [reference qualification read](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/117#issuecomment-5670665596) is incomplete pending the explicitly selected Milan descriptor profile. Exact-image provenance, calibrated pin/wire correlation for the same full sample, and INTERNAL/CRF evidence are still required. Existing digital acceptance and the common setpoint law remain as delivered by #435.

[A10] Dependency landed: kebag-logic/milan-fpga PR #449 (#447, the shipping TDM8 render lane) merged on dev as 0a3a78a9. The product image can now render the eight received channels at the TDM pins; the same-sample wire-to-pin measurement that this issue owns (acceptance 4, INTERNAL and CRF) is still the open physical step, unchanged in scope and schedule.

title: [Fabric] Deterministic listener latency: state the setpoint law for the shipping TDM render path and prove it on silicon
